ai.description: This gecko reaches 40 mm SVL. It is pale brown with dark crossbands and a granular, keeled dorsal texture. Distinctive features include a depressed head and a tail covered in whorls of enlarged scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus scabriceps* is uniquely identified by its strongly keeled, overlapping scales that give the body a rough, sandpaper-like texture, unlike the smoother-scaled *H. frenatus*.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus scabriceps* inhabits dry, scrubby deciduous forests and rocky outcrops in the Indian plains, often found under stones or within crevices in arid landscapes.
ai.behavior: The Scaly Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects and spiders while utilizing its specialized toe pads to navigate vertical surfaces.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus scabriceps* is oviparous, laying a single, hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus scabriceps* is endemic to the Indian subcontinent, primarily inhabiting the dry plains and coastal regions of Tamil Nadu and southern Andhra Pradesh.
